A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their full text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching across revisions, moves, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original language-selection experiments, automatic and human corpus evaluations, and MT training and fine-tuning results, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds data-size experiments, GPT-4o test-set comparisons, and additional COMET results.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o translation, segmentation, language filtering, alignment, and pivoting pipeline is retained, as are the model architectures and Appendix C training procedures. Naming heliport as the HeLI-OTS interface adds implementation detail without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: The seven target languages, 39-language pilot, Europarl and HPLT coverage, and Finnish–Somali/Finnish–Ukrainian directions remain unchanged. FLORES is relabeled FLORES+, but no additional language, domain, or task coverage is reported. The data-size sweep uses subsets of existing data.

E2.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o to the downstream full-test comparisons in Tables 3 and 7; v1 evaluated it only in the language-selection pilot. Other comparator sets are retained. EMMA becoming EMMA-500 identifies the same cited model.

E3.justification: New Section 5.4 introduces cumulative training subsets from 10% to 100%, holding tokenization and hyperparameters fixed. COMET reporting also extends to the HPLT and Finnish comparisons. Existing training regimes and human-evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a systematic seven-language training-data-size analysis in Section 5.4 and Figure 2, absent from v1. It tests scaling and saturation, showing that additional synthetic data helps but gains diminish around 50–60% of the corpus.

E5.justification: Both versions report paired t-tests, 5,000 bootstrap resamples, and the same human-annotation counts, agreement measures, and correlations. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, or uncertainty estimates for its learning curves.

E6.justification: V2 adds learning curves, GPT-4o ChrF/COMET test results, and COMET results for existing HPLT and Finnish experiments in Appendix E. Table 5 also changes Finnish-to-Somali NLLB-ft from 42.26 to 42.21 and Ukrainian-to-Finnish OPUS-MT-ft from 53.46 to 53.30, with corresponding delta changes. Existing English-direction scores and pilot scores are retained.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theory or proofs. V2's explanation that 21 × 7 yields 147 language pairs restates the existing pivoting construction rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add training-data-size analysis and scalability to the stated contributions. The central claims concerning synthetic-data usefulness, fine-tuning, HPLT complementarity, pivoting, and SynOPUS remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of diminishing scaling returns and competitiveness with GPT-4o, plus source-contamination and generation-cost limitations. The existing test-contamination warning is moved and expanded with a domain-mismatch argument. These qualify and extend the retained interpretation that synthetic data is particularly useful for poorly resourced languages.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies the pilot's development split, ChrF signature, COMET checkpoint, heliport interface, Finnish corpus sizes, and approximately $5,000 generation cost. It identifies Europarl v8syn, adds baseline-model access information, and updates the SynOPUS access destination. These are disclosures, not evidence of changed existing training settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds Iyer et al. (2024), Zhu et al. (2024), and de Gibert et al. (2024) to contextualize multilingual adaptation and HPLT. The main related-work positioning remains. Updated Llama and data-laundering references correspond to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose corrections, standardizes terminology, adds explanatory appendix introductions and acknowledgments, and inserts Section 5.4. The contamination discussion moves from Ethical Considerations to Limitations. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds learning-curve Figure 2 and COMET Tables 8–9, and extends Tables 3 and 7 with GPT-4o rows. Table 6 is enlarged and alphabetized, improving readability without changing its scores. Existing quality plots and annotation guidelines are retained, with relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical completeness through the controlled data-size study, GPT-4o comparisons, and additional COMET results. Clearer appendix presentation and new implementation, access, cost, and contamination disclosures improve transparency. These are useful, bounded gains to an otherwise retained study; contamination remains unresolved, and the new scaling curves lack run-to-run uncertainty reporting.
